newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo, Slovenia banks to start payment operations.
newsitem.headline: Yugo, Slovenia banks to start payment operations.

text.p: Direct bank payments have been restored between Yugoslavia and Slovenia as Belgrade-based Jugobanka has opened an account with Slovenia's Abanka d.d., banking officials said.

"We have opened accounts in three currencies -- U.S. dollars, German marks and Slovenian tolars -- which means payment operations in these currencies can go through these accounts," Marina Nesic, Jugobanka credit and correspondent relations manager, told Reuters.
Payment for goods and services traded between Slovenia and Yugoslavia will from now on be direct and simplified without mediation of third, foreign banks, she said.
Nesic said interest was growing among Yugoslav and Slovenian firms to renew economic cooperation following normalisation of relations between the states of the former Yugoslavia.
The National Bank of Slovenia issued a permit to the Belgrade bank in keeping with a new law allowing Yugoslav organisations to open pre-approved accounts.

Payment operations will apply to the period after December 16, 1995, or after the suspension of sanctions against rump Yugoslavia. The payment operations only cover current business and do not include previous transactions.
Abanka was Jugobanka's former subsidiary in Ljubljana before the breakup of the former Yugoslav federation in 1991.
Cooperation could be extended to include other banks, depending on interest, Nesic said.
